subject: Post-demo: Security & subprocessor scope clarification for HealthSync
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@healthsync.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.inference, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Security & subprocessor scope clarification for HealthSync

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Great conversation — I wanted to capture a short recap and the security/compliance items you asked for so we have a single place to track next steps.

Quick recap (from our side)
- Demo focused on private deployment options + dedicated capacity for PHI-sensitive flows.
- You asked about SOC 2 attestation, GDPR/HIPAA coverage, and a full subprocessor roster for cloud services that will see customer data.
- HealthSync procurement/security asked whether we can complete your vendor questionnaire and share evidence (SOC 2 report, data flow diagrams).

Requested next steps
1) Can you confirm whether your primary concern is PHI in transit vs. PHI at rest? That will determine whether you need Private (on-prem/VPC) or Dedicated.
2) We will share our subprocessor summary and SOC 2 attestation.
3) If you can send the HealthSync security questionnaire, we’ll start filling it and aim to return within 48–72 hours.

I’ve attached a short subprocessor summary to kick off the conversation (Redwood_Subprocessor_Summary_2027-07.pdf).

Planned internal owners: Ben (contracts/entitlements) and Karthik (security/compliance support). I’ll coordinate the vendor questionnaire return and a technical call if needed.

Would you be available for a 30-minute security deep-dive on Wed AM PST? If so I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Redwood_Subprocessor_Summary_2027-07.pdf
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@healthsync.com, procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Security & subprocessor scope clarification for HealthSync

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the PDF. Quick answers up front: the primary concern is PHI at rest and in transit; we need clarity on where tokenized personal data and PHI may be staged or cached (KV cache behavior), and whether any third-party analytics or monitoring services ingest logs that could contain identifying material.

Deliverables we need from Redwood to proceed:
- SOC 2 Type II report (or planned SOC 2 timeline if not yet available).
- Complete subprocessor roster including cloud infra, monitoring/telemetry vendors, analytics, logging, and any third-party inference accelerators.
- Filled copy of our vendor security questionnaire (attached: HealthSync_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx)
- A simple data flow diagram showing where PHI may transit/live for the hosted vs. dedicated vs. private options.

Timeline: procurement wants initial artifacts by Thurs COB (PST). If you can commit to a delivery window, that will let us move to legal review.

Also — does Redwood offer an on-prem package where no logs leave the customer VPC? If so, include that in the data flow.

Cheers,
Alex
Sr. Product Ops | HealthSync
alex.jones@healthsync.com

Attachment: HealthSync_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: Security & subprocessor scope clarification for HealthSync

Ben / Karthik —

FYI, forwarding Alex’s reply and the attached questionnaire. Procurement wants artifacts by Thurs COB PST. Can we commit?

Action items I’m proposing:
- Ben: Own the subprocessor roster and confirm which vendors are in logging/telemetry paths. Please pull the latest inventory and mark any vendor that may see token/KV cache material. (Deliverable: subprocessor roster CSV)
- Karthik: Pull or confirm our latest SOC 2 Type II report and redact as needed. Also confirm whether we have a pre-built PHI data flow diagram for Dedicated vs. Private.
- Laura: Can you help with the vendor questionnaire mapping (security/legal) and identify any escalations (e.g., if they require a written BA)?

I’ll respond to Alex with a proposed delivery window after we align internally. If we can turn around a draft questionnaire in 48 hrs, we can hit their timeline.

On Tue we should also decide whether to offer a technical call (security + infra) vs. simply sending artifacts.

Onward —
Marissa

Marissa / team —

We can hit the Thurs COB window with a staged delivery. Proposed split:
- Wed EOD: subprocessor roster (CSV) + high-level mapping of which vendors touch logs/KV cache/analytics. I’ll flag any that require an addendum.
- Wed EOD: draft vendor questionnaire (we’ll fill the easy sections and mark legal-only asks). Attachment: Vendor_Questionnaire_Redwood_DRAFT.xlsx (will share comments inline).
- Thu AM: SOC 2 Type II (redacted) and a one-page data flow diagram (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private). Karthik to confirm redaction scope.

Notes/assumptions:
- Our hosted deployment uses third-party monitoring (SignalMon) for infra metrics; logs are redacted but some metadata is retained. Will call out explicitly.
- KV cache is in-memory on the serving nodes; for hosted we persist shards for autoscaling — we should confirm whether persistence counts as 'at rest' for their policy.

Karthik: can you confirm whether we have an existing PHI diagram we can adapt? If not I’ll ask infra to sketch the flow.

Laura: happy to have you drive the questionnaire review and mark items that must go to legal or security for detailed responses.

I’ll assemble the CSV and the draft questionnaire and upload to the Drive link Marissa provided.

Ben

Ben flagged a couple of items we’ll call out explicitly (third-party monitoring vendor and KV cache persistence for hosted). Karthik will confirm redaction scope on the SOC 2. Laura will review questionnaire answers and escalate any legal-only items.

I’ve attached a mutual action plan for visibility (Mutual_Action_Plan_HealthSync_Redwood.docx) and will add the artifacts to the Drive folder once ready.
